results.title: CMS Transmittal 1875 - Consultation service codes no longer recognized for Medicare payment
results.text:
# Medicare consultation code elimination, January 1, 2010

## Policy change

Effective January 1, 2010, Medicare stopped recognizing consultation service codes 99241-99245 and 99251-99255 for Part B payment under the physician fee schedule. The change was applied budget-neutrally across inpatient and office/outpatient settings, with limited exceptions for telehealth consultation G-codes.

## Rationale

CMS restructured evaluation and management (E/M) payment. The transmittal states that the agency increased the work relative value units (RVUs) for new and established office visits and increased payment for initial hospital and nursing facility visits. These increased values were also carried into practice expense and malpractice calculations and into the E/M component of global surgical codes.

## What to bill instead, by setting

AI. Follow-up visits use codes 99307-99310. Nurse practitioners, clinical nurse specialists and certified nurse midwives may perform initial visits where state law permits and collaboration and supervision requirements are met. Office and outpatient: physicians and qualified nonphysician practitioners choose a new or established patient visit code (99201-99215) based on visit complexity and the patient relationship. A new patient is one who has not received professional services from the physician or physician group practice within the previous 3 years.

Critical Access Hospital Method II: appropriate new or established visit codes (99201-99215) are reported on type of bill 85X with revenue codes 96X, 97X or 98X for physicians and nonphysician practitioners with reassigned billing rights.

Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers: consultation codes were discontinued in favor of office visit codes (99201-99215) and nursing facility codes (99304-99306) as appropriate.

final_text:
**Claim 1652852** (outpatient) has a denial probability of 0.949. The validation-set average is 0.1805, so this is 5.26 times the average, or 76.8 percentage points higher. The denial label in this project is synthetic, so this is the probability of a constructed label and not a real payer decision.

**What the model weighs**
- **HCPCS_CD = 99241** is the "procedure/service code billed". It accounts for almost all of the score: 4.627 log-odds, with an odds change of 10125 percent. This is a CPT code, and this project doesn't carry its description.
- The other features are small. ORG_NPI_NUM adds 0.065 and PRVDR_NUM adds 0.042. The principal diagnosis Z733 (Z73.3, "Stress, not elsewhere classified") lowers the score by 0.061. ORG_NPI_NUM is undocumented in the project data dictionary.
- 153 features are not shown.

**What to check before submitting**
CMS Transmittal 1875 says Medicare stopped recognizing consultation codes 99241-99245 for Part B payment from January 1, 2010. That range includes 99241. For office and outpatient settings, the document says to choose a new or established patient visit code (99201-99215) based on visit complexity and the patient relationship. It also says the documentation must support the code chosen.

The policy documents don't say whether this payer or this claim has other exceptions.
